# ART_REDO.md — the art that is PRESENT and in the wrong dialect

[ART_ASSETS.md](ART_ASSETS.md) asks whether a file is there, and since D296 the
answer is yes for all of them. This asks the other question, which no manifest
can: **does the file agree with the game around it?** (D268)

Every number below is measured off the installed files each time this is
regenerated, so a set that has been re-rolled leaves the table on its own. The
*why* is [ART.md](ART.md) §8; this is the work list.

| set | files | mean luma | ink | over 0.80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enemies/`  ← **the bible** | 35 | 0.30 | 31.4% | 1.7% |
| `iso/foe/` | 70 | 0.34 | 26.6% | 3.4% |
| `powers/` | 30 | 0.35 | 25.2% | 2.7% |
| `relics/` | 38 | 0.35 | 24.0% | 3.1% |

The bible measures **0.30 mean luminance and 31.4% ink**. A set that is far
from both is not a matter of taste — it is a set drawn to a different brief.

## 1. The 30 power sigils — the only set left that is not painted at all

Flat vector clip art: one thin uniform stroke, flat fill, saturated primaries.
They sit on the Powers screen and on the run header, so the player meets them
every turn. Measured **0.35 / 25.2% ink / 2.7% blown** against the bible's
**0.30 / 31.4% / 1.7%**.

**Ask for a painted OBJECT, not a symbol** — the thing the power IS, drawn the
way a relic is drawn — held to mean 0.30 with a 2-3px ink outline and nothing
over 0.80. Six to a sheet.

Install: `godot --headless --script tools/install_sheet.gd -- powers <sheet.png> --key --cols=3`

## 2. The 38 relic icons — right brush, wrong value

The technique is correct and the VALUE is wrong by a measured margin:
**0.35 / 24.0% ink / 3.1% blown**. They are also all lit from the upper left
with a bright rim, which fights the one-saturated-source rule the rooms are
built on.

This does not need 38 new subjects. It needs the same objects re-asked at the
game's value: **dark, one accent, ink at 2-3px, nothing over 0.80**, and checked
against a BLACK ground rather than the generator's field — which is where a pale
object hides.

Install: `godot --headless --script tools/install_sheet.gd -- relics <sheet.png> --key --cols=3`

## 3. Two single files

* **`iso/shop.png`** — cream and white stripes, the brightest object anywhere on
  the isometric floor, and it is a shop rather than a light source. Re-roll it
  dark with one warm accent.
* **`iso/wander_0_s.png`** and its three siblings — the rat fills a fraction of
  its 128x192 canvas where the other wanderers fill it, so it renders small for
  a reason that is in the FILE rather than in `SPRITE_H`. Measure the bounding
  box against the canvas before re-asking (D288).

## 4. Six drawings that have no id table

The last of the computed dressing (ART.md §8a). Unlike the sixteen props and the
four landmarks, these have no table of names to key on, so the filenames have to
be chosen before anything can be briefed — which is the step D282 stopped at.
**Check for a table first:** the landmarks looked like this and `ISO_LANDMARKS`
had named them all along (D296).

| what | drawn in code today |
|---|---|
| the mark on a pushable wall (D182) | a crack with a pale bleed |
| the back door (D206) | a slab outline |
| the shrine | a polygon |
| the ledger | a polygon |
| the way down | nested diamonds |
| a key lying on the floor | a drawn key |

They are last on purpose: one drawing each, on one tile, seen when the floor
happens to lay one out. Item 1 is thirty files on a screen opened every run.

## What is NOT on this list

The 12 dungeon backdrops, the 35 enemy plates, the 70 creature fronts, the ~100
card faces, the 4 wall materials (D281), the 16 dressing props (D286) and the 4
landmark caps (D296). Those measure at or near the bible and everything above is
asked to match them. The UI kit is computed rather than painted (D83), which is a
decision rather than a gap.
